Not what I was hoping for. I was hoping for a game with a lot of puzzle solving, and while a few of the puzzles took a bit of creativity, there just wasn't enough of them. The game is a lot more focused on telling its story than it is on the puzzles. There's nothing wrong with that, but I didn't find the story that engaging, and the long stretches of dialogue slowly typing in chat boxes, and artfully blurry (and unskippable) cut scenes, bored me. I didn't get the "good" ending, at least I'm assuming I didn't, but I don't care enough to sit through all of that for another try.

The game puts you in the shoes of an FDI operator (ingame version of FBI), helping field operatives behind a computer screen.
There's a huge conspiracy you stumble into, aided by a hacker.
Without going into story spoilers, I saw the "twist" from the very start, obfuscated by a small wrinkle that doesn't actually play into the story at all unfortunately.

The game leaves many loose ends, and ends rather abruptly and is rather short overall (playtime 4,4 h on steam).

After finishing it it was obvious the game was very constrained by budget, and story wise seems the devs bite off more than they could chew or had much bigger plans for it. For that reason, the game kinda ends on a cliff hanger and your "choices" don't really matter, there is only one ending- my bet is that they want to make a sequel if this sells enough copies.
With all that being said, there is some amazing atmosphere, voice acting and tense and well written moments to experience in this. I'd love to see what the devs would be able to cook up given more room/time/money/people to breath and spread their wings.

I recommend it to people that like these desktop/hacker/operator type games - you can compare it to watching a really interesting thriller at the movie theatre - both in the cost of the game, and time playing it.

This is a well executed game with a quality UI and sound design. My only criticism is that the developers took a lot of care into designing the game's computer mechanics but then do not give you very many opportunities to use them. I was looking forward to a puzzle solving/detective type experience where I could piece together clues and solve cases, however the game's story quickly takes center stage; just as the tutorial section of the game ends, and you think that you'll now get to work on a wide variety of cases, you come to realize the entire game is more or less a guided experience through a conspiracy story. 

I personally was hoping for a more subtle, open-ended experience that focused on case solving, where the conspiracy itself could be discovered by a clever player gradually and then pursued as a personal choice. What is offered is entertaining and engaging, but those looking for a good detective experience will be somewhat disappointed.

[H2]Loved the game and the story line![/H2]

HOWEVER, it seemed like the developers kind of ran out of ideas for cases, there was one case with the chemscan function, only a couple with the HumanDB and only one case where the CarDB had good use. You also had an unforeseen event, in which I really enjoyed cracking. I would love to see more cases like these, more bomb cases, more cases where you have to dig a little through both Human and Car databases, and maybe even gett more information through these databases; like financials, past lives or past owners etc.. I would also love to see an endless mode where you get to just sit and solve new cases.

I completed the game and wouuld love to continue playing it, however as I have completed it, there is nothing more for me to do. The game is essentially dud to me now.

To work on; 
- Longer story line
- Harder cases for us to crack (can be adjusted through difficulty scale maybe?)
- Endless cases for replayability / for us to continue playing after completing the story line.

Can't wait to see your roadmap, as well as seeing where the future of this game goes!

5/5 Stars - A Gripping Investigative Experience: "The Operator" Sets a New Standard

I dove into "The Operator" blind, and emerged thoroughly impressed. This indie gem has raised the bar for investigative games, offering an engaging and immersive experience.

Standout Features:

- Interactive research mechanics: dive deep into case files, interview witnesses, and analyze evidence
- Innovative investigation system: follow leads, connect dots, and solve crimes
- Challenging puzzles: keep you on the edge of your seat

"The Operator" masterfully weaves storytelling and gameplay, making you feel like a real detective. The attention to detail and realistic scenarios create a captivating atmosphere.

Pros:

- High replayability
- Realistic investigation mechanics
- Engaging storyline

Cons: None notable

If you're a fan of investigative games or looking for a unique gaming experience, "The Operator" is a must-play.

Highly Recommended!
